name: Lazarus Pharmaceuticals Coagulant Bloom Injector — 'The Bridesmaid'
product_name: Lazarus Pharmaceuticals Coagulant Bloom Injector — 'The Bridesmaid'
description:
The Coagulant Bloom Injector is a single-use autoinjector loaded with a proprietary Lazarus compound designated LP-Heme-7, a synthetic fibrinogen catalyst suspended in a thermally-reactive polymer gel. Upon injection into or adjacent to a wound site, the compound undergoes rapid phase-change, expanding into a semi-rigid foam matrix that mechanically occludes hemorrhaging tissue while simultaneously triggering accelerated platelet aggregation. The entire process takes between four and nine seconds depending on wound depth and vascular involvement, with the foam matrix remaining stable for six to twelve hours before enzymatic breakdown begins.

What distinguishes the Bridesmaid from older field coagulants is its dual-action delivery: a hollow-bore needle deposits the compound deep into cavity wounds while a secondary ring-port floods the surface simultaneously, addressing both internal bleed and external seepage in a single press. The injector casing is constructed from recycled Palladian impact-polymer, matte white with a red grip band — the color scheme that gave it its street name, worn at the threshold between life and death like a bride at the altar. Medics note that the foam sets with a faint organic smell, somewhere between blood and antiseptic, which combat personnel describe as unmistakably associated with survival.

The Bridesmaid is ubiquitous in low-tier field medicine across GLMZ's outer districts. Street surgeons carry them in bundles of six. Corporate security medics carry them as backup to more sophisticated trauma systems. It is the piece of equipment most commonly pressed into the hands of someone who has never used medical gear before and told simply: find the hole, press the button. Its simplicity is its legacy.

specifications.contraindications: Incompatible with Helix Biosystems Hematic Sentinel Array — consult field manual

tactical_use: The Bridesmaid is deployed immediately upon identifying a hemorrhaging wound in a field context where surgical intervention is unavailable. The medic or even an untrained bystander locates the primary bleed site, positions the injector tip perpendicular to the wound, and depresses the grip trigger. No calibration or diagnostic step is required. In combat situations, it buys the window necessary to extract a casualty to a more capable medical station. Experienced medics use multiple units on complex wounds, staging injections across bleed sites in priority order. It is not a cure — it is a pause.
cultural_context: In the outer districts where Lazarus Pharmaceuticals dominates the medical supply chain, the Bridesmaid occupies a near-mythological status as the object that keeps people alive long enough to matter. Its white casing and red grip are immediately recognizable, and carrying one is considered basic civic responsibility in high-violence neighborhoods — the equivalent of knowing how to apply pressure. Among street surgeons and fixers it is a commodity of goodwill: leaving one behind after a job, or pressing one into someone's hands before a dangerous run, is a gesture that carries genuine weight. The name 'Bridesmaid' has been adopted as slang for anyone who keeps others alive without getting credit.
known_users: Anyone who has been in a firefight more than once
story_hooks: A batch of counterfeit Bridesmaids has entered circulation in the Sallow Ward — the compound sets correctly but begins dissolving at 90 minutes instead of 6 hours, and people are dying hours after being stabilized.
A Lazarus Pharmaceuticals internal memo suggests LP-Heme-7 contains a passive biomarker that flags treated individuals in corporate medical databases — someone is selling that data.
A street surgeon running a free clinic in the outer districts has run completely dry of Bridesmaids and is asking a crew to do a supply run that Lazarus will not sanction.
A character finds a Bridesmaid in the pocket of a corpse — the injector has been used but the body shows no wound. What was it used on?
related_entities: Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Space Elevator Tether System

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, pen-like autoinjector with a utilitarian medical aesthetic. The cylindrical body tapers slightly toward the needle end, with a pronounced red grip band occupying the lower third that contrasts sharply against the matte white casing. The design reads as deliberately simple and ergonomic—meant to be gripped and deployed by untrained hands under duress.
physical_description.dimensions: 14cm length, 3cm diameter—roughly the size of a thick marker or large syringe, easily palmed or clipped to gear
physical_description.weight_description: 87g—light enough to pocket or carry in medical pouches; handheld, no strap required
physical_description.primary_material: Recycled Palladian impact-polymer; the casing shows subtle stress-fracture patterning from the recycling process, visible under close inspection
physical_description.finish: Matte white with a semi-textured surface for grip security; the red band has a slightly rubberized, non-slip finish
physical_description.color_scheme: Clinical white body with a striking arterial-red grip band and transparent amber viewport showing the gel suspension inside; minimal branding in dark gray text
physical_description.interface_elements: Transparent amber viewing port running the length of the cylinder (shows gel viscosity and fill level); large red plunger head at the cap; subtle depth-marking ring around the shaft at 2cm intervals for insertion-depth guidance; single recessed safety lever on the side
distinctive_features: Dual-bore needle configuration visible at the tip: a central hollow-bore surrounded by a ring of smaller surface ports
Faint amber glow from the thermally-reactive gel visible through the viewport in low light
Organic, slightly iridescent quality to the gel interior—suggests biological activity
Aggressive ergonomic grip band with slight knurl texture
Small black safety lever positioned for easy thumb-release
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS embossed in dark gray on white casing; regulatory stamps for GLMZ Tier compliance; lot number and expiration date printed on the amber viewport band
physical_description.condition_typical: Fresh units appear pristine and clinical; field-worn examples show scuff marks on the white casing, occasional blood residue on or near the needle guard, and discoloration from exposure or impact. In active use, a faint organic smell—blood and antiseptic—emanates from the injection site within seconds.
